the minimum number of edges in a k-vertex-connected spanning subgraph of a k-vertexconnected graph is equal to the number of edges in the spanning subgraph with the property that the minimum degree is equal to the connectivity.

for every tournament T, every spanning subdigrap h with minimum inandout-degree at least 2 has at least n + 3 arcs, and every k-arc strong tournament contains a spanning (k+1)-arc-strong subgraph with at most n + 3k arcs.

every k-ark-strong tournament T has a spanning k-ark-strong subdigraph H with |E(H)| ≤ (k + 1)n − k 2 + 280k 2 and that every spanning subgraph H of T with minimum in-degree at least k contains at least |E(H)| ≥ (k + 2)n − k 3 arcs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the minimum number of edges in an m-arc-strong spanning (sub-)digraph is equal to the maximum number of edges in a spanning (sub-)graph with minimum inand/or out-degree at least m.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the minimum number of edges in a spanning subgraph of a k-connected graph is not necessarily equal to the minimum of the number of edges in all spanning subgraphs of the graph in which each vertex has degree at least k.
the number of arcs in the spanning k-arcstrong subdigraph of a k-arc- strong tournament is bounded above by the number of arcs of a k-vertex-connected subgraph of the tournament.
in the case of spanning k-arcstrong subdigraphs, the k-arc-strong property is much weaker than the property that every arc is contained in a directed cycle.
